title: Inside Hayden Panettiere’s troubling final months after a life in the spotlight | CNN
text:
Source: CNN

The untimely death of Hayden Panettiere, a onetime child star who soared to fame while navigatingaddictionandpostpartum depressionin her adult life, came just months after the beloved actor described feeling ready to start over.

Though she became a household name on television and film, Panettiere faced the sometimes-unforgiving glare of Hollywood’s spotlight, describing her experiences with domestic violence, motherhood and loss under intense scrutiny.

Now, as her family, friends and fans mourn, questions remain about what happened in the actress’ final hours before herdeath at age 36, far from her California home at an apartment in South Carolina.

Here’s a look back at Panettiere’s life and career:

At just 11 months old, Panettiere appears as aninfant in a Playskool toy train commercial— the first of many times she is placed under the spotlight.

Panettiere, then 7, joins the cast of the soap opera “Guiding Light,” playing the popular role of Lizzie Spaulding. The show, which Panettiere worked on until 2000, was thelongest-running television drama, focused on several families in the fictional Midwestern town of Springfield.

Panettiere later says theextreme plot lines— she played a child who got kidnapped, killed another character and survived leukemia — were not “good for my developing brain.”

“Subconsciously, I began to associate catastrophe with adoration,” she wrote in her memoir, “This Is Me: A Reckoning,” which released earlier this year. “People loved me when make-believe bad things happened to me.”

Panettiere plays the role of Gen Harwood, a competitive teenage figure skater whose mother, played by Kim Cattrall, also serves as her coach in Disney’s “Ice Princess.”

Her character initially serves as a rival toMichelle Trachtenberg’scharacter before the two eventually become friends. Trachtenberg died in 2025 at 39 from complications of diabetes mellitus.

At 17 years old, Panettiere lands her breakout role on “Heroes,” a critically acclaimed network television show about ordinary people who have extraordinary superpowers.

She plays an invincible cheerleader named Claire Bennet, a central character on the NBC drama, with the tagline, “Save the cheerleader, save the world.”

While many viewers praise the former child star as the beating heart of the series, her newfound success comes with heightened tabloid scrutiny, thecoverage wading into everything from her looks to her love life.

The rising star joins the cast of “Nashville,” thesoapy primetime dramain which she plays Juliette Barnes, an emerging yet troubled country singer.

The show features storylines about alcoholism and postpartum depression — topics that hit close to home for Panettiere at the time, she would later say.

Panettiere performed multiple songs as Juliette throughout the drama’s six seasons, including recordings that made their way ontoBillboard’s country charts.

Panettiere gives birth to her daughter, Kaya, with former fiancé and boxer Wladimir Klitschko.

Shortly after, Panettiere struggles with postpartum depression, and her substance abuse issues resurface.

Shewould later describefeeling at the time like there is “something seriously wrong with me.”

“I wish somebody told me it’s okay if you give birth to your child and you’re not immediately like, ‘Oh my god, I love you more than anything in the entire world right now.’ It’s okay and not abnormal,” she says.

Panettiere sends her daughter to live with Klitschko in Ukraine, a decision she called “the hardest thing I ever had to do.”

“But I wanted to be a good mom to her – and sometimes that means letting them go,” she says.

In May, a Brian Hickerson is charged in California with a felony count of “Injuring a Spouse, Cohabitant, Fiance’s, Boyfriend, Girlfriend or Child’s Parent,” according to documents from the Superior Court of Los Angeles County Clerk’s Office.

Panettiere later wrote in her 2026 memoir about a relationship that escalated into domestic violence by a man she referred to only as “Brian.”

Hickerson, after a plea agreement, isconvictedof two felony counts of “Injuring a Spouse, Cohabitant, Fiance’s, Boyfriend, Girlfriend or Child’s Parent,” in connection with offenses dating back to May 2019, according to the Superior Court of Los Angeles County Clerk’s Office. He would be sentenced to four years of formal probation, according to the clerk’s office.

Panettieretells Peoplethat when she was 15, someone on her team beganoffering her “happy pills” before red carpets – “to make me peppy during interviews,” she says.

“I had no idea what door that would open for me when it came to my addiction.”

Jansen Panettiere, Hayden Panettiere’s brother and a voice actor, diesat age 28 from an enlarged heartwith aortic valve complications.

“There was nothing in my life that feels like losing my other half,” Panettiere tells podcaster Jay Shetty in a 2026interview.

“We were so close, and being the older sibling – who it’s your job to protect them and keep them safe – and not being able to, heartbreaking doesn’t even begin to cover it.”

Hayden Panettiere says she has “been dealing with an injury for the past year,” in an interview withWomen’s Health. She describes experiencing “some nerve damage” in her lower back and “feeling nothing but pins and needles” from her waist down.

Panettiere appears on Jay Shetty’s “On Purpose” podcast, where she opens up about themes discussed in her memoir “This Is Me: A Reckoning,” including the challenges of being a child star and her struggles with addiction.

Panettiere also discusses the separation of her parents when she was 18 and how her motheralso served as her manager, blurring the lines between family and business.

Panettiere tells Shetty she and her mother no longer speak. “There is not a relationship between her and I, sadly.”

But despite what she’s been through, she tells Shetty she feels like she has “shaken off all of this darkness and this negativity.”

“I feel like I have a lot more life to live,” she says.

Just three months before her death, Panettiere releases her candid memoir detailing the progression of a once-exciting, new relationship that quickly escalated into years of domestic violence.

The actress writes about heated – and often drunken – arguments that ended with “Brian” slapping and hitting her between screams: “One night he busts up my face so badly I don’t leave the house for weeks.”

“You never forget the first time someone slaps you,” she writes. “Nor do you forget the last,” she says.

Panettiere writes aboutat least three different instancesin which “Brian” was arrested after he’d hit her during a fight, including on Valentine’s Day in 2020 while the couple was on vacation in Wyoming.

In May 2026, Brian Hickerson speaks withTMZabout Panettiere’s memoir and acknowledges that he “had a lot to drink, and I got physical with (Panettiere), and I got arrested” on February 14, 2020.

He calls the parts of the book detailing domestic violence “my chapter” and says, “Everybody should read it.”

Medics respond to a 911 call around 1:51 p.m. at a residence in Greenville and find Panettiere incardiac arrest, according to the Greenville County Coroner’s Office.

Dispatch audio obtained fromBroadcastify.comsuggests a possible overdose and CPR in progress, though authorities have not addressed whether an overdose actually happened.

A Greenville police officer arrives and interviews brothers Brian and Zach Hickerson, who said they called 911, a police report states. “I spoke with Zach Hickerson first. He advised this was his brother’s girlfriend,” the officer writes in the report.

Emergency personnel attempt to resuscitate Panettiere, but she is pronounced dead at the scene at 2:32 p.m., according to the coroner’s office.

Zach Hickerson later told TMZ in a statement the brothers had tried waking Panettiere up from a nap in the living room when they noticed she was unconscious.

“I immediately called 911 and Brian gave her Narcan. We then jointly performed CPR while 911 was on speaker until Fire and EMS arrived,” he said. “At that point we watched as they tried every measure possible to save her life.”

That day, Brian Hickerson shows the officer a bag of Panettiere’s medications, the police report said. But many details of the police report are redacted, including a list of Panettiere’s medications.

The responding officer says he was wearing a body camera during the incident, though the footage has not yet been publicly released.

An autopsy reveals no signs of trauma that would have contributed to her death, the coroner’s office said.

Panettiere’s official cause and manner of death have not been determined, as additional testing results are pending. Toxicology tests, which are standard in many death investigations, can take weeks to complete.

Tributes to Panettiere pour in from past colleagues, includingViola Davis,Kim CattrallandRosie O’Donnell— along with many others.

“What an amazing talent you were….so gifted,” Davis writes on Instagram. “I wish the world had more time with you because I had a burning curiosity about who you were becoming.”

Panettiere’s body is released to the mortuary her family chose, the Greenville County Coroner’s Office says.

That same day, Klitschkowrites in a statement posted to Xthat the family is “going through a time of profound shock and grief” while processing Panettiere’s death.

“She built an incredible career through immense talent, while also facing the darker sides of a very demanding industry,” the statement says.

“Young and talented people like Hayden should not leave this world so soon,” it adds.

The federal Drug Enforcement Administration, which enforces the nation’s controlled substances drug laws,joins the investigationintoHayden Panettiere’s death, according to reports from theNew York TimesandABC News.

Authorities have not addressed whether Panettiere overdosed August 16.

Panettiere would have celebrated her 37th birthday on this day.

Klitschko pays tribute to the mother of their child in a heartfeltpost on X, saying instead of “celebrating the way we had planned, today we celebrate her life, her spirit and the love that she brought into this world.”

He thanks people for reaching out with love and support and concludes by wishing Panettiere a happy birthday and saying, “you are loved, you are missed, and you will never be forgotten.”

Federal authorities are looking into whether the actress obtained illicit — and possibly counterfeit — drugs from a dealer in Southern California, a source familiar with the investigation told CNN.

DEA agents and Los Angeles-area authorities have questioned several people about the circumstances surrounding the California resident’s death, the source said, and they are examining the possibility she may have died after taking a counterfeit pill that she believed was another substance.

The source said the pending toxicology testing will be critical in helping investigators determine whether she ingested a counterfeit narcotic, and how it may have interacted with any other substances in her body at the time of her death.

While investigators have conducted investigative activity in the Los Angeles area, where Panettiere lived, and in Greenville, where she died, the source said authorities would be examining any other geographic areas the investigation may lead them to.

CNN’s Alisha Ebrahimji, Dianne Gallagher, Lisa Respers France, Holly Yan, Jason Morris, Karina Tsui, Elise Hammond, Alex Stambaugh and Josh Campbell contributed reporting.
